decisions.reason: The assigned item defines a CMDP as model data, not an optimization theorem. Its finite MDP, initial law, discount, cost signals and real thresholds are complete tuple data. The immediately subsequent def-discounted-cost-constraint explicitly defines J_g, J_r and feasibility by every J_ci <= b_i. Neither the model definition nor its contract claims optimality, existence of a feasible policy, or pathwise safety. Separating model data from the expected-cost convention is logically sound.

def-finite-markov-decision-process explicitly requires a finite subset R of the real numbers. With nonempty S and nonempty action sets, transition normalization forces R nonempty. Therefore B=max_{rho in R}|rho| is finite and |r(s,a,rho,s′)|<=B. Probability finite-time transition weights imply each reward expectation has absolute value at most B, so lem-bounded-discounted-return-converges and lem-normalized-discounted-state-occupancy-is-probability give absolute convergence and |J_r|<=B/(1-gamma). The rejection overlooks an inherited hypothesis.

The CMDP inherits the finite real reward alphabet R from def-finite-markov-decision-process, hence |r|<=B=max_R|rho|<infinity. The probability-mass/convergence supplier applies to every Dirac initial law, giving |V_g|<=B/(1-gamma). The normalized finite action-value sum then satisfies |Q_g|<=B+gamma B/(1-gamma)=B/(1-gamma); A_g=Q_g-V_g is finite. This also covers gamma=0 and each bounded c_i. No unbounded reward is admitted by the interface.

The inherited reward alphabet is a finite subset of R, so r(s,a,rho,s′)=rho is bounded by max_R|rho| and is a valid specialization of bounded g. Independently checked the complete local performance-difference telescoping identity, the column-stochastic resolvent occupancy estimate, and the finite weighted Pinsker argument. The proof bounds the residual by epsilon times the occupancy l1 change and obtains the coefficient 2 gamma epsilon/(1-gamma)^2. The KL branch preserves AC and explicitly treats infinite KL as trivial extended bounds, including zero error coefficients. No missing reward hypothesis or erroneous inference was found.

The rejection correctly identifies a presentation defect: both exact and one-state sampled KL equal K=(1/5)log(20)+(4/5)log(80/99)<4. The actual disagreement is exact CPO cost feasibility (1/5>1/20) versus the conditional safe-row sample cost check (0<=1/20, sample probability 99/100). Retitled the item to name this cost-check disagreement and synchronized its manifest title. The Example and all proof steps remain unchanged; no claim that the sampled quadratic program produces this proposal is made.
